pullRequests.head: claude/pensive-wozniak-x52913
pullRequests.body:
A Tauri 2 desktop app in launcher/ that puts OpenRAC behind buttons for every version in games/ (rac1 PAL and NTSC-U, rac2, rac3, rac4): find your discs, place each build's inputs, set up, build, check, play in PCSX2, and open the level editor. It runs the checkout's own tools and streams their output; it hard-codes nothing a game.json already says.
This is scaffolding: the app, its look, the catalogue, the job runner and the repository-wide actions work; most per-game actions are written from…

Summary
This takes OpenRAC from "play through emulation" to the scaffolding of a native PC port, built the way OpenGOAL ported Jak and Daxter, for every game version. It has three parts:

No emulation. The emulator experiment (runtime/) is removed. Its studies are kept in docs/port/, and git history keeps the code (for example at 7954152). The launcher no longer imports ISOs or runs anything emulated.
OpenGOAL's disc set-up. tools/extractor.py copies and validates the player's disc, using…

commits.headline: docs(policy): the top level is GPL-3.0-or-later
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
OpenRAC's own code (tools/, docs/, the top-level files) and the shared
runtime and renderer that will be added had no license. They are now under
the GNU GPL v3 or later (COPYING), chosen 2026-10-08; code adapted from
another project keeps that project's notice. The games' and the editor's
own licenses are unchanged. Open question 1 now only asks how code moves
between games whose licenses differ.

Verified: tools tests pass (Homebrew python3).

commits.author: Veradictus

The first piece of the shared runtime: the hardware contract the games

- src/ps2/gs: registers, primitive assembly (points, lines, strips, fans,

commits.headline: feat(runtime): a vector unit interpreter, and VU1 behind VIF1
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
src/ps2/vu runs microprograms with the timing they are written against:
the upper and lower instruction of a pair read the same state and the
upper one's register write wins; MAC, status and clip flags become
visible four instructions after the one that set them; Q and P arrive
when the divider and the function units finish, or at WAITQ and WAITP; a
conditional branch tests an integer register as it was before the
instruction right ahead of it; XGKICK sends its packet one instruction
late; the…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): openrac-vuscan, the interpreter against every game's VU1 programs
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A tool that finds the VU1 microprograms in an executable from the user's
own disc (runs of VIF codes beginning FLUSH, MPG), loads each through
VIF1 as the game would and checks that the interpreter decodes every
instruction pair. It prints counts and any instruction words it does
not know, never the programs.

Run on the five supported builds, all with nothing undecoded:
RAC1 PAL and US 9 programs and 8,625 instructions each, RAC2 10 and
10,086, RAC3 11 and 10,804, RAC4 13 and 10,996. The…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): the console's single-precision arithmetic as an integer model
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
src/ps2/fp.h computes add, subtract, multiply, divide, square root,
conversions and comparisons on raw bit patterns by the console's rules:
exponent 0 is zero, exponent 255 is an ordinary number, results are cut
to 24 bits, overflow gives 0x7FFFFFFF, the adder keeps one bit of the
smaller operand below the larger one's last place. The vector unit uses
it in place of host floats with a rounding mode, so its results no
longer depend on the host and overflow has the console's value.

The rules are…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): an EE interpreter and the machine around it; RAC1 PAL boots
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
src/ps2/ee: the Emotion Engine's CPU as an interpreter over guest
memory: MIPS III with the EE's additions (128-bit registers, the
multimedia instructions, the second multiply unit), the FPU on the
console's arithmetic (fp.h), and the vector instructions on VU0,
including microprograms started with VCALLMS. No kernel and no TLB:
SYSCALL and hardware accesses are handed out.

src/sys: the machine a program needs around that core.
- machine: the memory map, the DMA controller (VIF0, VIF1 with the…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): VU0 beside the EE; RAC1 PAL reaches its title screen
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The games use VU0 as a coprocessor that runs while the EE feeds it: a
microprogram spins on an integer register until the EE writes it. So a
microprogram started with VCALLMS now runs beside the EE, advanced when
the EE next touches VU0. The moves between the two wait as the hardware
does: with the interlock bit, a move from VU0 waits for the program to
end and a move to VU0 for the next instruction the program marks with
its M bit; an operation on VU0 itself waits for the program to end.

A…

commits.headline: fix(runtime): pipeline stalls in the vector unit, Z writes, mipmap addresses
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Three things the retail title screen and main menu showed.

- The vector unit is timed in cycles, not instructions. A float register
  written by one instruction can be read four cycles later; a pair that
  needs it sooner, or needs the divider while it is busy, waits, and the
  flags, Q and P arrive by the same clock. The games' microprograms are
  scheduled around this and read their clip flags by it: without the
  waits, some triangles of the title world came out as long streaks.
- With the…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): a silent sound server; RAC1 PAL starts a new game and runs level 0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The sound library's remote calls are now answered command by command:
the batch format (a count, then each command's number, size and data)
is read, streams and sounds get handles, a stream is reported buffered
at once and nothing is ever still playing. The game restarts a stream
whose start returns no handle, and its level start waits for the first
stream to be buffered, so a server that answers nothing useful hangs
it.

With this the retail program goes from the main menu through New…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): draw on several threads, decoded textures, faster inner loops
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The title loop of RAC1 PAL goes from about 7 to about 13 frames a second
on an M5 Max, with the same picture bit for bit.

GS:
- Primitives can be gathered and drawn by a pool of threads, each taking
  bands of 16 scan lines (Gs::set_threads; openrac-boot --gs-threads).
  A band's primitives are drawn in order, a band of a triangle computes
  what the whole triangle would, and what is waiting is drawn before a
  primitive that reads what it would write or writes what it would
  read, before the…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): skip flags no VU1 instruction can read, cheaper rounding switches
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
- None of RAC1's nine VU1 programs reads the MAC flags and five read no
  status flags (openrac-vuscan now counts the readers per program). The
  vector unit, when told to (VU1 only: VU0's flags are the EE's to
  read), does not work out the flags of an instruction when no
  instruction can see them: no reader between it and four cycles after
  the next instruction that sets flags, on the straight line, with any
  branch, delay slot or end of program in that stretch counting as a
  reader.…

commits.headline: fix(runtime): a branch after a flag read tests the new value
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The games' VU1 clipping code reads the sign flag of two plane tests into
two integer registers and branches on them in the next instruction. The
branch was given the value from before the second read, so triangles
crossing a clip plane were cut against the wrong side and came out as
screen-filling fans (the teal triangle over Veldin).

The instructions that read flags into an integer register finish early,
and a branch that had to wait for a float register no longer sees the old
value either.…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): play in the window: keyboard and game controller, one frame per field
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The window reads the keyboard and the first game controller into the pad
the games read, and runs no faster than the console. openrac-boot with
--window runs until the window is closed, and --report prints the speed.

The README says what runs now and how to run it; the milestones in the
design are marked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): switch the host's rounding only when it has to change; fields in flight, not registers
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Every vector instruction the EE runs switched the host's rounding mode
twice, and writing that register is slow. Each side now asks for its mode
on entry (reading the register is cheap) and nobody switches back. The
first level goes from 11.5 to 12.6 frames a second.

An arithmetic instruction marked all four fields of its target as in
flight, also those it did not write, so a later reader of the other fields
waited when the console's would not. Only the written fields are marked
now, as for…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): the drawing path on a thread of its own
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
On the console VIF1, VU1, the GIF and the GS run beside the EE: a program
hands the DMA controller a display list and carries on with the next
frame. The machine now does the same. The EE's side copies what a channel
or a FIFO write sends, in order with the writes to the GS's privileged
registers and the vertical blank; a second thread takes the copies. What
the EE's side needs back (a register read, pixels sent back, the picture)
waits until everything given has been done, and the EE's side…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): only the texture levels a primitive can read count
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The games leave the levels they do not need unloaded, with addresses that
point anywhere: often at address 0, which is a frame buffer every other
frame. Every level's pages counted as read, so a primitive drawing to that
buffer looked as if it read what it wrote and was drawn alone.

A primitive's levels now follow from the level of detail at its vertices.
A level is decoded on the thread that gathers primitives when a state
first needs it, so the drawing threads no longer share a lock, and…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): the GS draws batches in the background
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Primitives are gathered into a batch that owns everything they refer to
(states, colour table copies, decoded texture levels). A full batch goes
to a thread that draws batches in order, sharing each one's bands out
among the pool, while the next batch is gathered: VU1 no longer stops
while the GS draws.

A batch being drawn touches only the pages it draws to and the textures
it reads in place. Whatever else reads or writes GS memory (a transfer, a
colour table load, decoding a texture, the…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): the GIF and the GS on a thread behind VU1; colour and depth in one memory
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The drawing path is three stages now: the EE's side, VIF1 with VU1, and
the GIF with the GS. A packet VU1 kicks is copied (its length is read
from its tags) and taken apart on the GS's thread; privileged register
writes, the vertical blank and the picture go the same way, in order.
The first level runs at about 34 frames a second.

A game clears a buffer by drawing depth values into the memory it then
draws colours into. The two are laid out differently, so one row's depth
is another row's…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): openrac-vubench, the vector unit on a frame of a game's own display list
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
openrac-boot --dump-vif FRAME FILE writes what VIF1 is given in one frame,
with VU1's memories as they were before it. openrac-vubench gives that to
VIF1 again and again, times VU1 alone and prints a sum over everything VU1
sends and its registers, so a change to the interpreter can be timed in a
second and shown to compute the same.

The file is game data and stays on the machine that made it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): a vector unit pair in 9.5 ns instead of 14.6
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Measured with openrac-vubench on a frame of the first level; the sum over
everything VU1 sends is unchanged.

- Each instruction's function is found once per place in program memory:
  the four switches are instantiated with their selector fixed, so nothing
  is decoded while a program runs, and the arithmetic is one function per
  operation, operand source and target.
- What is worked out about program memory is kept for each content the
  memory has had. The games swap programs in and out…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): a frame read as a texture counts for the part that is read
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The games read the 512 by 448 frame as a texture declared 1,024 square.
Its pages as declared reach the other frame buffer and the start of the
texture area, so every other frame the blur passes looked as if they read
what they drew to (and were drawn alone, after waiting for everything),
and texture uploads waited for them. With texel coordinates the part a
primitive reads is known: only that counts now.

Also: after a batch is handed over because colours would meet depth
values, the state is…

commits.headline: perf(runtime): primitives that read what they draw to go to the drawing thread too
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A batch of its own kind holds them and is drawn one primitive after the
other, each top to bottom, so the thread that gathers no longer waits for
everything before it and draws them itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): the picture is copied in its turn; colour tables load for indexed textures only
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The thread that gathers primitives waited at each frame's end for the
drawing to finish, to copy the picture out. The copy is now a job among
the batches, done by the drawing thread when it gets there.

A TEX0 with a format that has no colour table does not load one. It did,
from wherever its unused address pointed (address 0, a frame buffer), and
waited for the drawing there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): a colour table is loaded when it is used
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A TEX0 can name a colour table that nothing is then drawn with, at an
address that points anywhere. Loading it at once meant reading memory a
frame was still being drawn into, and waiting for that. The load is now
put off until a state uses the table, a later load does not replace it, or
the memory it would read is about to be written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): large indexed textures are decoded too
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A 512 by 256 sky in an 8-bit format was read in place because of its
size, so the next frame's uploads to that memory waited for it to be
drawn. Only a large texture in a format a frame can have is read in place
now. Also: a batch of self-reading primitives no longer counts its decoded
levels as read in place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): VU0 skips flags nothing reads, as VU1 does
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The EE reads VU0's MAC and clip flags after its own vector instructions,
which always work them out, and what a microprogram leaves when it ends is
kept. Reading the status flags, whose remembering bits depend on every
instruction, turns the skipping off for good; these games never do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: perf(runtime): no wait check where no register can be in flight
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A float register can only be in flight from one of the last three pairs
run. Where none of the three pairs before a pair in memory writes what it
reads, and it was reached in a straight line, the check is skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(runtime): the memory card is a directory of the host
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The thirteen card library functions the game calls are answered from a
directory: a folder on the card is a directory in it, a file a file. What
they take and give follows the game's own card code, which checks every
result, and the library's public interface.

With it Ratchet & Clank (PAL) offers to create its save, writes its eight
files (350 blocks, as it expects to find them), shows the five slots,
saves a new game, and on the next start lists the save with its time, date
and level picture…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): music and speech: the sound library's streams are played
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The streams are plain ADPCM files on the disc that the program names by
sector. They are decoded and mixed one field's worth after each field, so
what the program is told (still playing, time left) and what is heard
agree, and a run gives the same sound every time. A file stitched on
behind a playing stream follows it under the same handle, which is what
the game's music code expects; a repeating file repeats until something
is stitched on.

The window plays the sound; --wav FILE writes…

commits.headline: docs(runtime): music and speech in the README and the milestones
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(runtime): the games' stash on the second processor; the pause menu opens
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The game parks its compressed HUD texture banks in the second processor's
memory (SifSetDma) and fetches them back through a small server of its own
when a menu opens. That server was answered like the sound server, so
nothing was parked, the unpacker found no header and trapped. The machine
now has that memory, SifSetDma copies into it, and server 0x11 tells where
the stash is and copies out of it.

When the program counter leaves memory the machine says so once, with the
last jumps and calls,…

commits.headline: style(runtime): the layout of runtime/.clang-format on every source file
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The tool's output and nothing else: four spaces, 100 columns, braces on
every body, the include groups. The objects of src/ built before and
after are byte for byte the same, and the tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: style(runtime): case bodies on their own lines
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The tool's output with the final .clang-format (a case label no longer
shares a line with its statements). Objects of src/ unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: docs(runtime): coding conventions for the C++
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
How the runtime's C++ is laid out, documented and commented: ten rules
that can be counted against a diff, then each area in detail, a section
for reformatting existing code and a self-check list. The layout part is
runtime/.clang-format.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(runtime): sound effect banks, scripts and voices
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The games' sound library plays sound effects from banks: each sound is a
short script of steps (tones, waits, loops, random picks, registers,
modulators) advanced 240 times a second, and each tone is a voice with
the sound processor's sample format and envelope.

src/snd holds that side of the library as a player of its own, adapted
from the 989snd reimplementation in OpenGOAL (ISC, Ziemas; see
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). It is not connected to the machine yet.

openrac-sndbank lists a bank from a…

commits.headline: refactor(runtime): a bank file's length comes from the bank reader
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A program names a bank on the disc by its first sector alone. The rule
for finding the length in the file's table was in the listing tool; the
machine needs it too, so it moves to Bank::file_bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: docs(runtime): doc blocks and comments across the model, first pass
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Every file of the runtime gets its file comment, and most types,
functions, members, branches and literals the comments the coding
conventions ask for. No code changes: every object of src/ is
byte-identical to the build before the pass (Release, -g0), and the
tests pass.

The pass is not complete. Still to do, as the files are next worked
on: the tail of vu.cpp, parts of ee.cpp and ee_mmi.cpp, and
tests/test_ps2.cpp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(runtime): sound effects play in the game
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The sound server now loads the banks a program names (from a sector of
the disc, or from the program's own memory), starts their sounds,
changes, pauses and stops them, and mixes them over the streams after
each field.

In Ratchet & Clank (PAL) the menu's ambience and its beeps play, and
the first level's sounds. Two runs give the same picture and the same
sound file. The picture at a given frame differs from before in the
hero's idle animation, because the game now sees its sounds…

commits.headline: fix(runtime): interrupt handlers and callbacks run on a stack of their own
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A handler or a disc callback that breaks into running code was given a
stack just below the interrupted code's stack pointer. Ratchet & Clank
has a routine that uses the stack pointer for something else while it
runs; a callback arriving inside it wrote its frame to nowhere and
returned to address 0.

The console's kernel runs handlers on its own stack. Here they now start
at the top of the first megabyte of main memory, the kernel's, where no
program is loaded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): Ratchet & Clank (US) runs, with a table made from the PAL one
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
tools/port_hooks.py finds each replaced library function of one program
again in another by the shape of its first instructions, with what
depends on link addresses masked out. All 54 entries of the PAL table
were found in the US program; two card functions that look alike were
told apart by their neighbours, one of them by hand.

With that table the US disc boots to the main menu and into the first
level, with sound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Interrupt handlers and the disc callback were called with whatever the
interrupted code had in register 28. Game code uses that register for
other things in places, and a handler that reads its globals through it
then read and wrote nowhere: Going Commando waited for ever for its DMA
handler to clear a flag, and the first game had stray accesses that
showed up as unknown hardware registers.

The pointer is now recorded when a handler or the callback is added and
given back for the call, as the…

commits.headline: feat(runtime): Going Commando (US) boots to its menu and its first level
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The table of replaced functions is the first game's, carried over by
tools/port_hooks.py: 45 of 54 were found, the other nine are functions
this game does not have in that shape and runs without. Its movie
player, found by the message it prints, is answered as skipped.

commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
runtime/tools/run.py configures and builds the runtime on first use and
then runs the tests, or starts a disc image in a window with the game's
table and field rate. It looks for CMake and Ninja beyond PATH, where a
desktop app's environment does not reach.

Run on macOS (Apple Silicon) with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin: 'run.py test'
ended with '100% tests passed, 0 tests failed out of 3'; 'run.py play
SCES_509.16 DISC --no-card --frames 300' built, opened the window and
ran at 50.0 frames a…

commits.headline: feat(launcher): play in the OpenRAC runtime
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Every version gets a play-runtime action that runs runtime/tools/run.py
with the version's serial and disc: unverified for rac1/pal, rac1/ntsc
and rac2/ntsc, planned for rac3 and rac4, which the runtime has no table
for. A repository action builds the runtime and runs its tests.

The actions were not yet run from the desktop app. The same command
lines were run from a shell on macOS (Apple Silicon); see the commit
before this one. cargo test -p openrac-launcher-core: 16 passed. npm run
verify:…

commits.headline: fix(launcher): find a Python the tools run on, and refuse an older one
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A desktop app started from the Finder gets a short PATH, which on macOS
ends at the system's Python 3.9. The level extractor and the tools need
3.10: 'Extract the levels' stopped with a TypeError.

Python is now also looked for in Homebrew's and /usr/local's bin, a
Python that works is proposed before one that does not, and Settings
says why an older one is refused.

cargo test -p openrac-launcher-core: 17 passed, also with

commits.headline: feat(runtime): build a game's decompiled C as host code
commits.author: Veradictus

port/port.py compiles each source file of a decompilation to wasm32,
where pointers are 32 bits as on the console, translates it to host C
with wasm2c, and wraps every function so that calls cross the file's
edge through the EE's registers. The result is the library the runtime
loads with --native.

build, in about ten seconds. On the way to the main menu 124 of them
run, 242,000 calls, and the menu draws as it does…
